source_refs.note: Book p. 6: 1.4.1 Graph of Exponential Function (properties to study before sketching)

blocks.text: Before sketching the graph of an exponential function, we study its essential properties that determine its overall shape and behaviour. These include the domain and range, intercepts, injectivity, monotonicity, and asymptotic behaviour. Understanding these features helps us to predict the graph without plotting many points. After this analysis, we use a few representative values to draw a smooth and accurate sketch of the function.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
What the words mean:
Domain and range: the allowed inputs and the obtained outputs.
Intercepts: where the graph meets the \(x\)-axis and the \(y\)-axis.
Injectivity: whether the function is one-to-one (no output repeats).
Monotonicity: whether the graph only rises or only falls (strictly increasing or strictly decreasing).
Asymptotic behaviour: a line that the graph approaches but does not reach.
All five are proved for \(y = a^{x}\) in 1.4.2.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Sketching plan for any exponential graph (used in Examples 7 and 8):

items: Make a short table of values, e.g. \(x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\).
Plot the points and join them with a smooth curve that approaches the \(x\)-axis but never touches it.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Study the properties first; they fix the shape of the graph.
2. Then a few representative values are enough for an accurate sketch.
3. The five properties: domain and range, intercepts, injectivity, monotonicity, asymptote.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Joining the plotted points with straight line segments: the graph is a smooth curve.
2. Letting the curve touch or cross the \(x\)-axis: \(a^{x} > 0\) always.
3. Plotting only positive \(x\)-values: the domain is all real numbers, so show negative \(x\) too.
